entities.summary:
The Battle of Corinth was a pivotal engagement between the Roman Republic and Corinth, occurring on the Isthmus of Corinth in 145 BCE. 

 This decisive battle marked a turning point in the Roman conquest of Greece, as the Roman Republic ultimately emerged victorious, claiming Corinth as a key strategic location. 

 The repercussions of the Battle of Corinth rippled forward in time, significantly impacting the Roman Republic's expansionist policies and the subsequent Roman dominance over the Mediterranean. 

 As a testament to the enduring legacy of this battle, the city of Corinth would remain a crucial hub of Roman power and influence for centuries to come.
